nyciml-2005-06-fall-seniora-01.prompt: On Jeopardy, each contest matches three people. In a tournament, in each match there is always one winner and the winner advances to the next round and the other two players are eliminated. The tournament continues until only one person remains. If $243$ players enter the tournament, compute the number of contests that must be played to determine the champion.

nyciml-2005-06-fall-seniora-02.prompt: Triangle $GAB$ has sides $GA = 28$, $AB = 32$ and $GB = 40$. The altitude drawn to side $GB$ intersects that side at $H$. Compute $GH$.

nyciml-2005-06-fall-seniora-06.prompt: Donald Trimp is building a theater with $k$ rows. In the first row there are $15$ seats, $17$ seats in the second row, $19$ seats in the third row, and so on. Compute the smallest value for $k$ such that the number of seats is a perfect square.

nyciml-2005-06-fall-seniora-07.prompt: Compute the number of real roots that satisfy the equation: $5^{\sqrt{5-x}} = \left(5^{\sqrt{5-x}}\right)^x$.

nyciml-2005-06-fall-seniora-08.prompt: Isosceles triangles are cut off of each corner of an $8$-inch square. The resulting shape is a regular octagon. The area of the octagon may be expressed as $a + b\sqrt2$. Compute $a + b$.

nyciml-2005-06-fall-seniora-09.prompt: The sum of an infinite geometric sequence is $3$. The sum of the squares of the terms of the sequence is $\frac92$. Compute the common ratio of the original geometric sequence.

nyciml-2005-06-fall-seniora-10.prompt: A circle passes through the three points $N(-2, 2)$, $Y(6, 6)$ and $C(8, 2)$. Compute the length of the radius of the given circle.

nyciml-2005-06-fall-seniora-11.prompt: Compute all real values of $x$: $2x^2 - x - \sqrt{2x^2 - x - 6} = 12$.

nyciml-2005-06-fall-seniora-12.prompt: Working together, Ben and Jerry take $15$ hours to build a model car. Working together, Ben and Tom can build the same model car in $20$ hours. Working together, Tom and Jerry take $25$ hours to build the model car. Compute the number of hours it will take Tom, Ben, and Jerry to build the model car working together. (Assume that each works at a constant rate.)

nyciml-2005-06-fall-seniora-15.prompt: Two perpendicular chords intersect in circle $O$. One chord is divided into two parts of lengths $4$ and $6$. The other chord has a length of $14$. Compute the length of the radius of the circle.

nyciml-2005-06-fall-seniora-16.prompt: Four players, playing bridge, are each dealt $13$ cards from a standard deck of playing cards. Charles Goren has a hand with $9$ spades and $4$ clubs. Compute the probability that his partner, Grace Goren, has the remaining $4$ spades in her hand.

nyciml-2005-06-fall-seniora-17.prompt: Find the first set of three consecutive positive integers such that the smallest is a multiple of $3$, the second is a multiple of $5$ and the largest is a multiple of $7$.

nyciml-2005-06-fall-seniora-18.prompt:
Solve for all ordered triples $(p, q, r)$ if
$$\begin{aligned} 2pq + p + q &= 115\\ 2qr + q + r &= 49\\ 2pr + p + r &= 10\end{aligned}$$

nyciml-2005-06-fall-seniora-19.prompt: $a, b, c, d$ are non-zero real numbers. Compute all possible values of: $\dfrac{a}{|a|} + \dfrac{b}{|b|} + \dfrac{c}{|c|} + \dfrac{d}{|d|} + \dfrac{abcd}{|abcd|}$.

nyciml-2005-06-fall-seniora-20.prompt: Compute all possible values of the real number $k$ for which the following equation has one real root: $2005^x + k\cdot 2005^{-x} = 10$.

nyciml-2005-06-fall-seniora-21.prompt: $x^2 + 4hx = 1$ and the sum of the squares of the roots of the equation is $10$. Compute $h^2$.

nyciml-2005-06-fall-seniora-22.prompt: $\triangle ABC$ is an equilateral triangle with side $6$. $\overline{BC}$ is extended through $C$ to $D$ so that $\overline{CD} = 6$. If $E$ is the midpoint of $\overline{AB}$, and $\overline{DE}$ intersects $\overline{AC}$ at $F$, compute the area of quadrilateral $BEFC$.

nyciml-2005-06-fall-seniora-23.prompt: Compute the number of integral values of $x$: $\left|\dfrac{x+12}{x+2}\right| \ge 3$.

nyciml-2005-06-fall-seniora-24.prompt: Compute the right-most non-zero digit when $100!$ is computed.

nyciml-2005-06-fall-seniora-25.prompt: A fair coin is tossed repeatedly. Compute the probability that heads will appear four times before tails appears twice.

nyciml-2005-06-fall-seniora-26.prompt:
If $x, y, z$ are real numbers, compute all possible values of $x + y + z$:
$$\begin{aligned} x + y - z &= 3\\ xy + 9 &= 0\\ x^2 + y^2 + z^2 &= 27.\end{aligned}$$

nyciml-2005-06-fall-seniora-27.prompt: A box contains $4$ red, $5$ blue and $6$ white marbles. Compute the number of samples of four marbles, chosen randomly and without replacement, such that every color will be represented.

nyciml-2005-06-fall-seniora-28.prompt: In trapezoid $QUIK$, bases $\overline{QU}$ and $\overline{IK}$ have lengths of $15$ and $45$ respectively. The non-parallel sides $\overline{QK}$ and $\overline{UI}$ have lengths of $30$ and $20$ respectively. $\overline{AB}$, a line segment parallel to $\overline{QU}$ is drawn, with $A$ on $\overline{QK}$ and $B$ on $\overline{UI}$. $\overline{AB}$ divides the trapezoid into two trapezoids of equal perimeter. Compute $AQ : AK$.

nyciml-2005-06-fall-seniora-29.prompt: Compute the sum of the infinite series: $\dfrac{2}{8} + \dfrac{20}{8^2} + \dfrac{56}{8^3} + \dfrac{272}{8^4} + \dots + \dfrac{4^n + (-2)^n}{8^n} + \dots$

nyciml-2005-06-fall-seniora-30.prompt: A beetle walking on a Cartesian coordinate plane starts at the origin. It walks one unit up to $(0, 1)$. The beetle now turns $90^\circ$ to the right and walks $2$ units and then turns $90^\circ$ to the right and walks $3$ units. The beetle continues this process until it walks $2005$ units in one direction. Compute the coordinates of the beetle when it stops.
